Hi Liam — thanks for the clear ask. I put together two pragmatic paths and attached a short matrix and our latest pricing PDF. High level answers:

- Hosted -> Dedicated: yes, we preserve model config, routes, and telemetry. The Console supports pinning model versions and replaying traffic during migration; there is a small onboarding migration credit we can apply.
- Bundling embeddings+generation: we can create an "integrated pilot" bundle that offers blended unit pricing and shared cache benefits — useful for early-stage evaluation where token patterns are mixed.

Attached: HelixAI_Rollout_Matrix.xlsx and redwood-pricing-2026-v2.pdf

Conservative path (low-risk):
- Start: Hosted API, Standard Pilot Bundle (2 concurrent streams, 250k tokens/mo)
- Timeline: 3 months pilot, evaluate throughput/latency
- Upgrade trigger: sustained >80% of pilot throughput for 3 consecutive weeks
- Discount guide: 15% pilot credit + onboarding credit (1 month)

Aggressive path (scale-first):
- Start: Hosted API with reserved capacity holdback (burst to Dedicated pool for heavy runs)
- Timeline: 6–8 weeks to Dedicated if accepted
- Bundle: embeddings + generation blended SKU with 25% blended unit discount at commit
- Discount guide: pilot credit + 10% one-time migration credit if commit within 90 days

Two technical levers I recommend we highlight in the matrix:
1) Shared KV prefix caching when embeddings + generation used in same routes — this can reduce token spend by ~12–18% for typical retrieval patterns.
2) Reserved warm pools for model variants — if HelixAI expects bursty nightly jobs, we should recommend a small Dedicated warm pool (1–2 GPUs) to keep latency tight while keeping base costs low.

For the migration credit: legal prefers a committed migration window in the SOW (90 days) and a one-time credit equal to 5% of the first 3 months' committed spend. We can be flexible on phrasing (credit vs. invoice rebate).
